title: Cyprus Visa Information for Applicants in Serbia

embassy_in_serbia.name: Embassy of the Republic of Cyprus in Belgrade

visa_eligibility.serbian_citizens: Serbian citizens holding a biometric passport do NOT require a visa to enter Cyprus. They may stay up to 90 days within any 180-day period. The passport must be valid for at least 3 months after the planned date of return. It is not possible to obtain a visa or tourist pass at the border crossing.
visa_eligibility.other_nationals: Third-country nationals residing in Serbia must apply for a Cyprus national visa at the Embassy. Holders of a valid double- or multiple-entry Schengen visa, or a residence permit issued by a Schengen state, Bulgaria, Croatia, or Romania are exempt and may enter Cyprus without an additional visa (up to 90 days in 180 days). Turkish and Azerbaijani citizens must follow the regular visa procedure unless they are family members of EU nationals. Note: Cyprus is not a Schengen member state as of 2026, so a Cyprus national visa is required for those not covered by the above exemptions.

processing_times.notes: Normal processing time is 15 calendar days. May be extended up to 45 days if additional examination or documents are required. Applications may be submitted no earlier than 6 months before the intended travel date and no later than 15 days before arrival.

application_location.center: Embassy of the Republic of Cyprus in Belgrade
application_location.booking: Contact the embassy directly by phone (+381-11-3620002) or email (belgrade@mfa.gov.cy) to schedule an appointment. No VFS Global center identified for Cyprus visas in Serbia — applications are submitted directly at the embassy.

visa_fees.service_fee: Fees are non-refundable regardless of the outcome. Single-entry: €20; Double/multiple-entry: €60. The €80 Schengen-harmonised fee may apply in some missions — confirm current fee with the embassy in Belgrade.
fee_exemptions: Spouses and children under 18 of EU/EEA/Swiss nationals (with proof of relationship)
Holders of valid double/multiple-entry Schengen visas (no Cyprus visa required)

required_documents_all_applicants: Completed and signed Cyprus visa application form
Valid passport issued within the last 10 years, with at least 2 blank pages, valid for at least 3 months beyond the intended stay
Return country visa or residence permit valid for at least 3 months beyond the stay (if applicable)
Confirmed round-trip travel itinerary with fixed dates (flight bookings)
Hotel reservation or proof of accommodation for the entire stay
Medical travel insurance covering the full period of stay in Cyprus, minimum coverage €30,000
Proof of sufficient financial means: bank statements for the last 3 months
All documents must be in English, Greek, or Turkish; documents in other languages require a certified translation
additional_documents_by_nationality: Bank guarantee may be required (€200–€500 depending on country of origin) — requested at the consulate's discretion
Third-country nationals must demonstrate legal residence in Serbia (e.g. residence permit)

required: Certified written consent from both parents or legal guardians
Original birth certificate including parents' details, or court documentation (e.g. custody order)
documents_for_minors.note: Parents or guardians should be present during submission if possible. All standard documents listed under required_documents_all_applicants also apply.

tourism: Confirmed accommodation booking (hotel reservation or proof of property ownership in Cyprus)
Travel itinerary for the full stay
business: Official invitation letter from a company registered in Cyprus specifying purpose, duration, and host details
family_or_private_visit: Assumption of Responsibility form completed by the Cypriot host (available from the embassy)
Copy of host's Cypriot ID card or passport
Host's proof of address and contact details
medical_treatment: Letter from the medical institution in Cyprus confirming the appointment, treatment details, and expected duration
Proof of financial means to cover medical costs
transit: Onward travel documents (confirmed ticket to final destination)
Visa or entry permit for the final destination country (if required)

employees: Recent employer letter on company letterhead confirming: employment status, position, start date, salary, and approved leave for travel dates
entrepreneurs: Letter from a solicitor, accountant, or bank manager confirming self-employment or business ownership
students: Original letter from school, college, or university confirming enrolment and attendance
retirees: Pension book or official pension statement confirming monthly income

special_provisions: Cyprus is NOT a member of the Schengen Area as of 2026, though accession procedures are ongoing. Entry is only permitted through legal entry points: Larnaca International Airport, Paphos International Airport, Larnaca Port, Limassol Port, Latsi Port, and Paphos Port. Entry through ports or airports in the Turkish-occupied northern part of Cyprus is in violation of Cypriot law. ETIAS (European Travel Information and Authorisation System) is expected to apply to Cyprus from late 2026, including for Serbian citizens currently travelling visa-free — it will cost €7 per application (originally announced as €7, some sources cite €20) and will be valid for up to 3 years or until passport expiry.
